title: A complete sentence
explanation: A sentence expresses a complete thought. Find who or what the sentence is about, then what that subject does or is. An imperative may have an understood subject: you.
example: The researcher checked the figures. Subject: the researcher. Predicate: checked the figures.

check.prompt: Which sentence expresses a complete thought?
check.explanation: The subject committee has a finite verb, published, and the thought is complete.

task: Write one sentence about an action you completed today. Underline the subject mentally and identify its verb.
attribution: Original CSS Vista instructional example; not an authentic past-paper question.

stages.title: Understand the idea
stages.teach: Read the explanation and different worked example above. Answer this recognition question before writing. A wrong answer receives an explanation and can be retried.
stages.example: Choose the option that follows the taught distinction.
stages.question: Which option is defensible?

stages.title: Write independently
stages.teach: Apply the lesson to a sentence of your own. Keep your meaning; do not copy the worked example.
stages.example: For an access issue, name the actor and the specific action rather than writing only “Things should improve”.
stages.question: Write your first sentence.

stages.title: Review the wording
stages.teach: Identify the subject, verb and intended logical relationship. Check the relevant Grammar lesson. Optional AI feedback must target the saved wording, not your unsaved rewrite.
stages.example: A conditional claim should retain its if clause or an equivalent condition.
stages.question: What do you want the sentence to mean, and what needs checking?

stages.title: Revise independently
stages.teach: Rewrite using the lesson and any saved feedback. A new version preserves your earlier wording. You may retain wording you can defend; shorter is not automatically better.
stages.example: Compare who acts, what is claimed, the time frame and any qualification.
stages.question: Write your revised sentence.

title: Advanced sentence transformation
explanation: Change structure while preserving who acts, what is claimed, the time frame and qualifications. A passive construction or compressed clause must not strengthen the original claim.
example: Original: The team may finish the review if the missing files arrive. Equivalent: The review may be finished by the team if the missing files arrive.

check.prompt: Which revision preserves "The measure may reduce delays if staff receive training"?
options: The measure reduces delays without any conditions.
With staff training, the measure may reduce delays.
check.explanation: May and the training condition remain; neither certainty nor timing is invented.

task: Transform a conditional sentence of your own into a different structure. Check that its qualification and meaning survive.
attribution: Original CSS Vista instructional example; not an authentic past-paper question.
